question: A user asks Claude.ai to build a working single-page HTML landing page with embedded CSS that they can preview, tweak, and eventually export. Which output format best serves this request?
options: A) Choose an inline HTML code block because code blocks render identically to artifacts and provide the same live preview and export options.
B) Use a Mermaid diagram because diagrams are the standard way to represent the structure of a web page before writing any code.
C) Use a plain-text description of the page layout because writing prose about the design avoids the risk of embedding malformed markup.
D) Use an artifact because a single-page HTML site is self-contained, substantial, and the user previews and refines it outside the chat.
correct_answers: D) Use an artifact because a single-page HTML site is self-contained, substantial, and the user previews and refines it outside the chat.
explanations: Incorrect. Inline code blocks only display the code as text; they do not offer the live preview or one-click export features that artifacts provide, so they are not equivalent.
Incorrect. Mermaid diagrams are meant for flowcharts and diagrams, not for creating interactive web pages; they cannot fulfill the request for a working, exportable landing page.

Incorrect. A plain-text description of the page layout fails to deliver the functional, previewable HTML page the user explicitly requested, and writing prose does not mitigate markup risks better than actual code.

Correct. Artifacts are designed for self-contained, substantial content like a single-page HTML site, allowing the user to preview and refine the work in a dedicated panel and later export it for use outside the chat.
